title: The Fraud of the Belly-Speaker
english: This is intended to explain why the belly-speaker was said to be possessed, even though the Scripture contradicts him, as he himself partially admits locally. But why after these things did he add the prophecy he was discussing with the ruler? «The Lord will tear the kingdom from your hand and will give it to your neighbor, David; because you did not obey the Lord's voice and did not fulfill a wrathful anger against Amalek; because of this word the Lord has done this to you on this very day, and the Lord will give Israel with you into the hands of foreign tribes» (1 Sam 15:28-29).

If anyone wishes to clarify the matter precisely, he must first return to the historical context of the letter and, having unfolded that passage, see where, after having defeated Amalek, the king seized the best of the dogs [spoils] and thought it necessary to offer them as burnt offerings. By seeking more clearly and scientifically, one would have found that all these words Samuel had already spoken by word at that time; for he said that the Lord had indeed torn the kingdom from his hand, when the ruler, seizing the wing of the Philistine, tore it. He also foretold to him regarding these things how the kingdom was destined to be given to his neighbor, who would be better than him, and how Israel would be divided because of this and would no longer return.

Having said these things, he made the words consistent with the deeds; for not long after, having been appointed king by a divine judgment sent forth, David became king. Was the one said to be speaking through the belly-speaker, therefore, announcing anything new? The things said previously by Samuel he was merely mimicking as his own, deceiving by persona, or perhaps by technical skill, appearing to speak prophetically by repeating the same things.

But just as charlatans and soothsayers go to the houses of the wealthy, rushing in and exaggerating matters of life already passed to search for things hidden, they imply that they are speaking of things that happened long ago spontaneously...

title: The Deception of the Belly-Speaker
english: They stun those who listen, and they flatter those who are submissive regarding what they wish to happen in the future; thus also the appearance of the belly-speaker is transformed. On the one hand, it explained the prophetic sayings of Samuel, but it seemed to prophesy without knowing anything, but rather it proposed foreign things as its own and struck the interlocutor with amazement; because of these things, it easily stole and snatched away the mind of that person.

What then does it add after these things? 'And you,' it says, 'tomorrow, you and your son Jonathan with me, and the Lord will give the camp of Israel into the hands of other tribes' (1 Sam 14:44-45). But the demon was saying these things as if they were its own. It must be sought whether it was saying true things, as it seemed, and whether it announced them by chance and coincidence, and whether it was able to foreknow these things.

First, it does not appear that Saul was destroyed on the sixth day, as the appearance was saying. For if, having heard the words from extreme despondency, 'he did not eat bread all that day and all that night' (1 Sam 14:43), it says 'that day,' as the Scripture forbids the aunt, and after this, the woman, dissuading him, again urged him to prepare food, it is evident that on the second day, after that all-night and all-day fast, having been cast down to the ground in utter collapse, he rose and sat more decorously on the couch, while the woman, having taken the calf which she had carelessly, slaughtered it, preparing a meal and frying unleavened cakes, made the food pleasant.

Since she also brought to him and to those around him, having prepared it skillfully, the one himself took a meal at the table; it is necessary to understand that he had reached other nocturnal hours, if he had indeed departed from there by night. Thus, this thing itself proves the demon was lying; for it did not happen, as it said ('tomorrow' you will be 'with me'), as it had occurred.

title: The Deception of the Spirit
english: Thus, he had exhausted himself in such a way that he spent the day fasting, then, having taken a morsel of food on the second, he walked into the camp. It is not only striking in light of the facts as he spoke, but he also said that Jonathan would end up alone with his father (1 Sam 14:45); yet from the opposites, the narrative of the letter proclaims a voice [saying] that Saul was slain along with three boys, but not with only one, as he had said.

Surely the demon did not speak anything true by way of a foreknowledge (for he would not have announced things contrary to what happened), but, having diverted from what was previously said to Samuel, as I have said, he added a few things to these, weaving them similarly from the images. Thus also he threatened death to the ruler, by making use of those voices of his. But he even promised to introduce an interruption to Israel, because the prophet had said heavily that the people would be divided.

Seeing therefore the war-engines fortified and the leader of the people standing in distress, he also added [threats] regarding what was left to him of God (through which the ruler, speculating, confessed that the prophet's preaching was being circumscribed), and he responded to the incoming movements by shouting aloud. However, whatever he added of his own, he clearly having been caught lying; for he was not able to foretell even the day of death, nor the executions of the sons of Saul (1 Sam 14:47), of whom the Scripture mentioned by name. From these things, it would not be difficult to perceive that the spirit announced nothing of its own nor anything true, but as he subverted the words of Samuel, he thought he was prophesying by flinging them about.

But above all, it is not possible to say that he prophesied this without falsehood; for if indeed he proclaimed the occurrence of war and the unceasing streams of bloodshed, who is the cause of all wars? Is it not the devil? Did he not himself seek out Job (Job 1:12)? Did he not provoke war against him?
